images.title: First taste decision
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE standalone 3:2 landscape rough interaction study.
Low-fidelity UI wireframe of a desktop node-graph application, viewed flat and
straight on. Grayscale marker or pencil sketch on light paper, tidy but clearly
rough, like a whiteboard drawing by an interaction designer. One accent color
only, amber, for numeric signal. A second muted accent, violet, for picture
connections. Everything else gray. Picture previews inside nodes are simple
procedural patterns drawn roughly: checkerboard, concentric rings, soft blobs.
Nodes are plain rounded rectangles dominated by their preview, with no words
inside them at rest. Tiny pictograms mark signal kinds: a framed square for
picture, a single dot for pulse, a crosshair for position. Inputs enter on the
left edge, outputs leave on the right edge. Very little text. Use only the
labels the scene allows, in plain handwriting, and leave out any label you
cannot render exactly. Generous empty canvas. Interaction is shown by a simple
arrow cursor and, when the scene asks for it, a few numbered frames side by side.
Three numbered frames left to right showing the same canvas. Frame 1: an empty
canvas with a single arrow cursor about to click, nothing else. Frame 2: at
the click point, a loose fan of four rough picture swatches has appeared
(checkerboard, concentric rings, soft blobs, diagonal stripes), each large
enough to judge as a picture, with no names; the cursor hovers one of them.
Frame 3: the chosen picture now sits on the canvas as one node showing that
picture large, with a small quiet tick mark beside it meaning saved, and
nothing else around it. Allowed labels: "1", "2", "3", "saved".
No glass, chrome, metal, bevels, 3D perspective, drop shadows, glow halos,
neon, product-render lighting, tables or floors, hardware plugs or jacks. No
inspector panel, sidebar, toolbar, menu bar, parameter list, or sliders on
every node. No wizard dialog, Next button, OK button, or explore/goal mode
switch. No title, subtitle, slogan, caption, paragraph, header, footer, or
presentation-board layout. No waveform graphs. No text other than the allowed
labels.
Independent variation 1 of 3. Keep the specified interaction and all invariants; allow only modest differences in rough sketch composition. Do not write variation labels or scene titles.
images.judge:
does frame 2 read as results to choose between rather than a menu. Does
frame 3 look already usable with no further setup implied.
images.assessment: Partial: picture choices and a saved result are readable, but the 2×2 grid resembles a menu. Dark background and glow violate the style.
